eips.title: Dynamic individual consolidation incentive
eips.summary: Anders shared in chat as a new EIP for dynamic individual consolidation incentive to help reduce validator count.

moments.context: Anders linked EIP-8502 in chat in response to Barnabas saying the validator count should be trimmed as much as possible, noting he also has a capping EIP in preparation.

eips.title: Hardware and Bandwidth Recommendations
eips.summary: Referenced as the bandwidth requirements standard that gossip-sub aggregation traffic far exceeds.

moments.context: Kamil noted that aggregation traffic with gossip-sub sometimes hits 200-300 megabits, which is way beyond EIP-7870 limits even in its current form.
Mikhail framed simulation results using EIP-7870 node types (attester, local block builder) to describe bandwidth constraints.

eips.title: Fast Execution Payload Broadcast
eips.summary: Referenced as an existing Lighthouse implementation using Waggle for fast execution payload broadcast.

moments.context: Kamil noted that Lighthouse already has an EIP-8411 implementation with Waggle, suggesting they could port that approach for PQ proof messages.

eips.title: eth/XX - announce transactions with nonce
eips.summary: Cited in chat as an EIP improving networking for the traditional mempool.

moments.context: Csaba mentioned in chat that EIP-8077 is improving on the networking for the traditional mempool, in response to a discussion about whether the PQ networking stack should be reused for mempool transactions.

eips.title: In-mempool signature and proof aggregation
eips.summary: Cited in chat for the networking side of recursive aggregation.

moments.context: Csaba linked an ethresear.ch post on EIP-8288's networking side of recursive aggregation, replying to Barnabas asking whether PQ transactions are also bigger on P2P.

eips.title: Custom sweep threshold for validators
eips.summary: Discussed as a prerequisite for requiring 0x02 credentials, since it would let operators keep 32 ETH behaviour after migrating. Justin twice called it 8198 before Kev caught the slip.

moments.context: Barnabas said the staking operators' pushback on a 0x02-only rule would largely go away if 8148 is committed to.
Justin, saying 8198, asked whether it would resolve every operator's concerns; he understood it covered Lido's but not other staking operations'.

Justin asked whether disallowing new 0x01 deposits at H-star would depend on it, again calling it 8198; Kev asked whether he meant 8148, the Lido EIP, and Justin said he was mixing up numbers. Dustin also flagged 8148 in chat.
Mega noted in chat that with 8148, translating 0x01 deposits into 0x02 validators capped at 32 ETH would behave the same as 0x01.
